# ChatView: the assistant in your layout

<!-- Generated by dist/sdk/gen-widget-docs.py from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

The assistant as a component, its port, tools, context and the scripted test port.

## `chatview`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/chatview.rs`)

`ChatView`: the IYAKKI assistant as a component an SDK app places in its layout (docs/development/UI-SDK.md, "Embedding the assistant").

The app keeps a `ChatView` in its state, gives it an [`AssistantPort`] (the core's), a [`SessionConfig`] (a conversation name, the tools
the app offers, the context) and a rectangle to draw in. The view owns the conversation on screen: the transcript, the field, the
approval card, the model and role choice. It draws through [`Canvas`], so it works in the shell, in a browser or client (display
list) and as a WASM tile, with the colours and size class of the host.

What the app does, in four lines:
```text
event(Tick):   for inv in chat.tick() { let r = self.run_tool(&inv); chat.answer(&inv, r); }
event(Action): if chat.owns(a) { chat.action(a) }      event(Key/Text): chat.key(k) / chat.text(t) first
view:          chat.draw(c, th, &metrics, rect)         context changed: chat.set_context(items)
```
An app tool runs in the app, never in the view: the view hands out a [`ToolInvocation`] and the app answers it. A tool that asks has
already been allowed by the person (through the core) when the invocation arrives.

How many action numbers a chat view uses, from the base the app gave it.

```rust
pub const ACTIONS: u32 = 8
```

```

### struct `ChatView`

pub struct ChatView
```

Public fields:

Methods:

- `pub fn new(port: Box<dyn AssistantPort>, cfg: SessionConfig, action_base: u32) -> ChatView`
- `pub fn owns(&self, action: u32) -> bool`: Whether an action number belongs to this view.
- `pub fn busy(&self) -> bool`
- `pub fn pending_approval(&self) -> Option<&Approval>`
- `pub fn error(&self) -> Option<&str>`: The last refusal or failure as a sentence (also in the transcript).
- `pub fn wants_keyboard(&self) -> bool`: True while the field has focus: the host shows the on-screen keyboard.
- `pub fn set_context(&mut self, items: Vec<ContextItem>)`: Attach what the person is looking at now (replaces the earlier context).
- `pub fn send(&mut self, text: &str) -> bool`: Send a message as the person. A refusal (the assistant is busy, the core says no) is shown and the text stays in the field.
- `pub fn cancel(&mut self)`
- `pub fn answer(&mut self, inv: &ToolInvocation, result: Result<String, String>)`: Answer an app tool call (what the app did, or why it could not).
- `pub fn tick(&mut self) -> Vec<ToolInvocation>`: Read what the session says now (every tick while an answer is coming, every tenth tick otherwise) and return the app tool calls.
- `pub fn pump(&mut self) -> Vec<ToolInvocation>`: Read the events now and return the app tool calls that are ready.
- `pub fn action(&mut self, a: u32) -> bool`: A hit region of this view was used. Returns whether the action was ours.
- `pub fn key(&mut self, k: UiKey) -> bool`: A key. Returns whether the view used it (the app then does not). With the field focused every key is the field's; without it only `y` and `n` while an approval card is showing.
- `pub fn text(&mut self, t: &str) -> bool`: Typed, pasted or composed text for the focused field.
- `pub fn wheel(&mut self, d: i32)`: The wheel over the transcript (positive: towards older lines).
- `pub fn transcript(&self) -> Vec<String>`: The transcript as plain lines (for tests and a screen reader summary).
- `pub fn draw(&mut self, c: &mut dyn Canvas, th: &Theme, m: &Metrics, area: Rect)`: Draw the view inside `area` (never outside it). Radii, gaps, text sizes and shadows are the skin's (`m.tokens`).

### fn `wrap`

Break `s` into lines that each measure at most `max_w` (on words; a word longer than a line is cut). Empty lines of the text stay.

```rust
pub fn wrap(c: &mut dyn Canvas, size: f32, style: TextStyle, s: &str, max_w: f32) -> Vec<String>
```

## `assistant`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/assistant.rs`)

The assistant port: what an SDK app is handed so that it can embed the IYAKKI assistant (see [`crate::chatview::ChatView`]). Like the
storage port it carries no pixels and opens no socket: the host gives the app a port, and the port is the core's. One port is one
session (the person and the app are bound by the host), so no call names a session.

The host-side meaning, in one paragraph: the core owns the model, the history and the person's approvals. The app declares its own
tools (a name, a description, a JSON Schema, and whether the person is asked first); the model can call only those. An app tool runs in
the app: the port hands out [`ChatEvent::ToolCall`], the app does the work on its own data and answers with [`AssistantPort::answer`].
A tool that changes something is `ask: true`: the core shows a card and waits for the person ([`ChatEvent::Approval`]), and writes the
audit line. [`ScriptedAssistant`] is the in-memory port for tests and the browser preview: a scripted model that follows the same rules.

### const `MAX_TEXT`

The most characters a scripted fake keeps of a message (the real core has its own limits and refuses with a sentence).

```rust
pub const MAX_TEXT: usize = 8 * 1024
```

## `toolargs`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/toolargs.rs`)

The arguments of an app tool call, read without a dependency: the core hands an app the arguments as JSON text, an object whose
values are mostly strings, numbers and booleans. [`Args::parse`] reads one object (nested objects and arrays are kept as raw text),
with the strings unescaped. It refuses what is not an object, text that goes on after the object, and anything nested deeper than
16 levels, with a sentence the app can give the model back.

### enum `Val`

```rust
pub enum Val
```

Variants:

- `Str(String)`
- `Num(f64)`
- `Bool(bool)`
- `Null`
- `Raw(String)`: A nested object or array, as it was written.
